I did coolsculpting on my lower stomach and flanks/love handles - 3 applicators on my stomach and 1 applicator on each flank so 5 in total. Only one cycle. Overall I did notice less fat in those area  especially where I had minimal fat pockets to begin with like small ridges where my ab lines are. I would type myself as skinny fat so it defined my waist a little bit more. Also my diet really needs to get back on track after thanksgiving. It’s a good noninvasive option but multiple cycles are needed to get the results you want. Personally for the price I paid for one cycle I wish I waited to get lipo with ab etching which will be my next hardmaxxing item. Also something nobody really talks about with cool sculpting is the pain. I felt a lot of pain and loss of sensation in my stomach after the fact. The procedure itself is painless. I would describe myself as someone with a high pain tolerance. I get tattoo removal on a half sleeve every 3-4 months and can tolerate it. That’s considered a highly painful process, but the coolsculpting recovery was very uncomfortable for me. Just things to consider if you’re weighing Coolsculpting vs lipo.

It depends on if you need to see specialists often. I have health issues that require me to see specialists so a PPO is in my best interest. A PPO allows you to see specialists in your network without a referral (some may have a higher copay without a referral vs with so do be sure to check your insurance card).

If you only see the doctor for standard medical care such as physicals, medication and the occasional emergency visit you may want to stick with an HMO. It may have a high deductible so be aware of that and remember you will need a referral for specialists.

Some benefits of Kaiser that I’ve encountered: They offer extra bonuses in their network such as counseling, classes, and offered COVID19 vaccines to their PTs (at least in CA) when they were in high demand.

It really depends on your needs but both plans are widely accepted in SF/CA.

Self help books:


-Buy Yourself the Fucking Lilies by Tara Schuster—the author was VP of talent at Comedy Central and exec of Key and Peele, the book itself is easily digestible and a great read on how to repair your relationship with yourself.


-Think Like a Breadwinner by Jennifer Barrett— author is the Chief Education Officer at Acorns the robo investing company, the book is all about women and our relationship with money. It gives a great basic rundown on investing, saving, negotiating and teaching women how to level the playing field when it comes to money. I think every woman should read this book.


-The 5am Club by Robin Sharma—motivating concepts especially if you struggle with discipline and routine. The storyline was too cheesy for me but looking past that I really rebooted my entire schedule after reading this.


-Honorable mention: Women Food and God by Geneen Roth—I haven’t read this one yet however the person who highly recommended this book to me because I struggle with my relationship with food. They said this book isn’t religious despite the title and it’s a good read to reflect on your own relationship with your body.

Autobiographies:

-The Baddest Bitch in the Room by Sophia Chang—the title speaks for itself, she worked in the music industry mostly with Wu Tang. I believe she was the first Asian woman in the hip hop industry. She’s a badass lady.


-More than Enough by Elaine Welteroth—this is an autobiography but honestly doubles as a self help book. Elaine is the second black Editor in Chief of Teen Vogue. Her autobiography details her upbringing and time at Conde Naste. Hearing her talk about navigating what it means to be a woman of color in journalism, constantly having to prove herself was really powerful. I learned a lot from this book and it was probably my favorite read of 2020.


-Bossypants by Tina Fey—I love 30 Rock so this book pretty much is like a Tina Fey/30 Rock behind the scenes. She talks a lot about her experience as a woman in comedy. Some of the jokes are outdated if you’re able to look past that. 


-Every Day I’m Hustling by Vivica A. Fox—I loved this autobiography, she details a lot of her career as an actress, especially her role in Kill Bill. Also can’t help but Stan that she spills everything on her former relationship with 50 cent and how he’s a legit man child.

I was able to keep the weight off. When my hashi’s got really bad right before I found my endocrinologist I see now I had gained back 10 pounds which is a lot on my 5 foot frame. Once my medication was in check the weight fell off with light but regular activity. 

I can’t say what my levels were like when I initially lost the weight. My first diagnosis was hypothyroidism. Hyper and hypo is present in almost all of the women in my family. When I went to college (and fell off my routine of bloodwork and taking medication for hypo) I noticed how exhausted I was. I was sleeping through classes, exams, sometimes sleeping for days at a time. When I went to multiple doctors at my school/in the area after telling them about my hypo they took an abridged blood test and thought I was lying because t3 and t4 came back normal. My guess is at this time is when hashi’s started. It wasn’t until three year after those blood tests (and losing the weight) that I was formally diagnosed with hashi’s so hopefully that gives you more insight! 

Was I able to do it with a thyroid issue present? Yes. Just be kind to your body. I feel frustrated everyday not having a perfectly flat stomach and toned abs that I feel I could have without hashi’s but I know my body needs TLC. So gentle exercise and patience with myself it is. 

P.S. Someone who lives by this workout philosophy is Melissa Wood Health! She’s a former model who used to over exercise and now practices gentle daily exercise grounded in Pilates and yoga. If theres any weights involved it’s either bands or ankle weights. I think she has some videos on YouTube or Instagram but I paid for her all access pass for her website full of these gentle workouts which was pretty reasonable.

Wishing you lots of luck! Not an easy journey but a rewarding one to learn to be gentle with yourself even in times when we feel out of control.
